Regarding the notification received from the President about the convening of the session of the Federal Parliament.
Hon'ble Members, I will now inform you of the contents of the said notification.
Nepal's Constitution, Article 93, Sub-section (1), as per the recommendation of the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal dated Chaitra 16, 2082, the session of both houses of the Federal Parliament has been convened on Thursday, Chaitra 19, 2082, at 14:00 hours in the Federal Parliament Building, Singha Durbar.
(Ram Chandra Poudel)

Chaitra 16, 2082
To be presented for information.
Hon'ble Members, now let us stand for 1 minute in silence to pay tribute to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for democracy.
Hon'ble Members, I heartily welcome all Hon'ble Members on the occasion of the commencement of the 20th session of the Federal Parliament, National Assembly. The National Assembly, which began on Falgun 21, 2074, has already completed 19 sessions in 8 years. During this period, due to the active role of the Hon'ble Members, the National Assembly has succeeded in presenting a dignified image of a mature, judicious, coordinated, cooperative, and stable house. For this, I express high respect to the Hon'ble Members and praise their role.
As the National Assembly is a permanent house, one-third of the members' terms expire every two years, and elections are held proportionally. According to the constitutional arrangement, we bid farewell to 19 members in Falgun and have also formally welcomed 18 newly elected members. I once again heartily welcome the newly elected Hon'ble Members to the National Assembly meeting.
Hon'ble Members, we conducted the 19th session from Magh 4 to Falgun 1, 2082, amidst the Gen-Z movement and the subsequent political developments. Although short in duration, I feel that the 19th session was of great importance and dignity in terms of responsibility and work. Amidst the changed political situation of the country after the Gen-Z movement and the announcement of new elections following the dissolution of the House of Representatives, we completed specific tasks through the National Assembly amidst a kind of uncertainty. By resolving some legal complexities and by building mutual trust in accordance with the spirit of the constitution through agreement, cooperation, and coordination with the government, the Federal Parliament, political parties, and other stakeholders, and by dispelling the fear and uncertainty generated among the public, the National Assembly has been able to play a parental role, and I feel proud of this.
Hon'ble Members, significant changes have occurred in the country's political landscape from the conclusion of the 19th session of the National Assembly to the commencement of the 20th session. The Nepali people have given a new mandate through the House of Representatives elections held on Falgun 21. According to that mandate, the Rastriya Swatantra Party has secured a single majority, and a new government has been formed under the leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister Balendra Shah.
In a democratic system, the mandate expressed through the people's vote is supreme, and it is essential for the parliament and the entire state machinery to be accountable to that mandate. The public expects the new government to bring speed in good governance, transparency, accountability, effectiveness of service delivery, and development works. It is our shared responsibility to guide the government in the right direction through policies, laws, and oversight to address the public's aspirations and expectations. I express my belief that the role of the National Assembly will be equally important in this regard. We are all confident that the government will function lawfully and that public sentiment will be duly respected.
Hon'ble Members, the interrelationship, cooperation, and coexistence between the two houses of the Federal Parliament, the House of Representatives and the National Assembly, are the basis of democratic parliamentary practice. While the House of Representatives is the house of representatives directly elected by the people's vote, the National Assembly symbolizes the balance, continuity, and mature deliberation of the federal structure. If mutual coordination, respect, and cooperation between these two houses are strengthened, the overall effectiveness of the parliament will increase. Therefore, I express my belief that constructive cooperation, experience sharing, and coordination between both houses will be further strengthened in the coming days.
Hon'ble Members, due to the damage to the old parliament building in Banepa and the under-construction new parliament building in Singha Durbar not being fully completed, we have been compelled to conduct the assembly under challenging circumstances for some time. We will have to conduct this session from this very assembly hall.
We all expect that once the under-construction parliament building is completed soon, it will facilitate the operation of the assembly and parliamentary activities. Furthermore, the use of modern technology in the new building will help make the parliament's work more organized, transparent, and effective. I hope that parliamentary work will be further strengthened through the use of digital systems, archiving, information dissemination, and new technologies for conducting meetings.
Hon'ble Members, I have the belief that the experience and contribution of the newly elected Hon'ble Members who have come as members of the National Assembly from this session onwards will further enrich the work of the National Assembly. The Federal Parliament Secretariat is preparing an orientation program for the newly elected members with the objective of providing information about parliamentary practice, legislative process, the role of committees, and parliamentary dignity.
I expect this to help make parliamentary work more organized and effective. I believe that the Hon'ble Members will participate actively, constructively, and accountably in the legislative matters, policy issues, and national and regional concerns to be discussed in this house in the coming days. The beauty of democratic practice lies in healthy debate, diversity of thought, and agreement. Therefore, I also expect that the ideas presented here, based on the culture of moving forward with agreement, will be dignified, constructive, and focused on the public interest, just as in previous sessions.
It is extremely important for the parliament to guide the overall development of the country in the right direction through the government's policies and laws and to work towards improving the living standards of the people. In particular, the National Assembly has been making a significant contribution by meticulously studying and amending legislation and providing necessary suggestions from the perspective of long-term national interest. It is expected that the National Assembly will fulfill its constitutional duties and responsibilities even more effectively in this session. Our common objective is the welfare, prosperity, and good governance of the country's people. To achieve this goal, it is necessary today to rise above political differences and prioritize national interest.
Therefore, I also appeal to the Hon'ble Members to perform their roles in the parliament with dignity, responsibility, and positivity. I express my belief that the active cooperation and effective role of all Hon'ble Members will be instrumental in effectively conducting the National Assembly, and I extend my heartfelt best wishes for the complete success of the 20th session.
Hon'ble Members, in the context of the commencement of the 20th session of the National Assembly, representatives from the parties represented in the National Assembly have been given the opportunity to present their views. I will now provide time sequentially to the Hon'ble Members. First, Hon'ble Member Krishna Prasad Sitaula.
Hon'ble Shree Krishna Prasad Sitaula (Nepali Congress):- Mr. Chairman, today (14:15) we have reached a new political situation in Nepal. Elections have been held, and a new government has been formed. In this situation, we are holding a meeting of the National Assembly today. First of all, I want to congratulate all the new friends who have been elected to this house. There are no new friends, all the new arrivals... (Mike not heard) The decisions we make are mostly consensus decisions here, we don't have much of a 'for' or 'against' here. Even though there is a ruling and opposition, today only the minister is here. Tomorrow it might be different. One person is yet to be appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister. In today's context, what will happen after two years, who knows, but this session can do great work for the benefit of the country and the nation. In this sense, I extend my heartfelt best wishes for the success of this session. I also wish the government well. The newly elected government has come with new enthusiasm and new vigor. We want to cooperate with the government constructively on policy matters for the benefit of the nation and the people. There is a saying, 'Support good work, oppose bad work.' I want to say this a little differently: May the government always do good work, so that we can always support it and not have to oppose it. My best wishes to the government in the lower house and this house. May the government only do good work. Good work means for the benefit of the people, for the benefit of the nation, for further strengthening the fundamental aspects of this constitution, in its implementation, and in fulfilling the aspirations with which the people formed this government by giving a large mandate. May the government always play a constructive role in this regard. We will have a positive role in this. The country's independence, sovereignty, nationality, this constitution is a constitution of inclusive democracy. May the government move forward in ensuring that policies benefit all classes, regions, castes, genders, professions, and occupations, and all levels of government, local, provincial, and federal. I have many best wishes for the government in this regard.
I felt it necessary to raise one issue on this first day. The first decision of the government's first cabinet was very unusual and surprising to me. Some people in power might say, 'You are an old person, you have old ways,' but I have to say something today. The cabinet itself decided, 'Do not implement this part of the commission's report now, implement this part, arrest them, imprison them.' The cabinet decided this, and after that, what will the ministers do, what will the secretaries do, what will the government lawyers do? First, that commission should be officially published. It should probably be tabled in the house. Otherwise, it should be made public so that the general public knows. It only came out online, we found out online, others also... (Mike not heard) Yes, this decision of the government does not align with the spirit and essence of the constitution. Such hasty arrests do not align with the constitution; it has failed to follow the due process of law. I am a worker of such a party, the Congress. In the 2007 revolution, we took up arms, and the Rana regime ended. However, the country's late revered leader, B.P. Koirala, became the Home Minister, making the last ruler Mohan Shamsher the Prime Minister. We never believe in politics of revenge. We never believe in politics of retribution.

We do not. We believe in social harmony and unity. We do not believe in things that spread hatred in society, ... things that spread hatred, that do not build society or the nation. The country is currently at a juncture in its politics, and only by moving forward together in a balanced manner can the good of this country be achieved. That is what we believe in. Therefore, I just want to say that even more so, Prime Minister KP Oli, his body is also extremely sensitive, he has had kidney transplants twice. His body itself is sensitive. He was not in a hurry to flee, nor was he in a hurry to present evidence, just as the police handed over the urgent public property, surrounded the house overnight and arrested him in the morning. This was not appropriate at all. If he were to flee, his party would not contest the elections. He would not have contested the elections. He would have gone earlier, perhaps written a letter at home. There is a human aspect to such things, and the government could not understand that human aspect, nor did it consider us. We have reached this point after crossing many difficulties, after crossing many difficulties. That is why we have crossed many difficulties and reached this point. We have also been resolving every difficulty with an understanding. We have not yet reached a conclusion on many incidents. For example, some remaining tasks of the peace process, which are unjust, are still incomplete. Two commissions are still active. They are still unable to provide justice to people who have suffered injustice in the past 10 years. Work is still pending. If all of us, all political parties in the country, move forward unitedly without any sense of revenge or retribution, only then will this country prosper. We have seen many incidents in the past, such as achieving a majority in power, reaching nearly two-thirds. In 2048 BS, our own party had a majority, but it could not last for three and a half years. In 2056 BS, the Nepali Congress had a majority, but it could not last long. After the promulgation of this constitution, the leftists, with a two-thirds majority, slightly less than that, similar to the current situation, could not even last for three and a half years. Therefore, it is a time when we need to think very seriously about Nepal's politics today. Therefore, I want to urge the government, especially the Prime Minister, through the honorable minister, to build unity among us all and move forward. This unity is not for us, not for power, not for power sharing, but for the people, and we can build a common point in policy-making so that the nation can be moved forward together. There is the problem of employment, the problem of unemployment, many people have aspirations. How many millions of people are in the Gulf countries, there is war there. Our brothers and sisters living in the desert, what will be their condition? If we all think seriously and create a new policy, then we can address that issue. How much has our economy grown, what is our economic situation, how much budget will come, and we all know that it is a matter of building the nation. But all those things can be achieved through our broad unity and understanding, and the country can move forward. The current politics is not the same as it was five years ago. Now, America's stance on Iran, Ukraine and Russia, the bombing in the Gulf countries, the whole world is in a state of panic. Whether we Nepalis are anywhere in Europe, whether they are soldiers recruited in Russia, whether they are people in Ukraine, whether they are people in the Gulf countries, whether they are people who have reached Iran, even people who have reached America and are suffering due to America's changed policies, if we remember all of them, all of us Nepalis must stand together and build a new map for the country within this constitution. If we cannot do that, then conflict, a new kind of conflict, can be invited into Nepal. The outside world thinks that Nepal is always like this, but we should not let Nepal suffer. The suffering of the people, the happiness of the people, the prosperity of the people are all subjects of our common effort. I want to conclude my remarks by wishing the government special good luck. May the government always strengthen the constitution from within, implement the contents of the constitution correctly, work extensively for the benefit of the people, and build national unity. Sometimes, national unity is misinterpreted as seeking power sharing, which is absolutely not the case, never. In a parliamentary system, there is a government and an opposition. There is support for the good work done by the government and opposition to the bad work. Therefore, as I said at the beginning, it would be fortunate if the situation where the government has to be opposed never arises, and with this wish, I conclude my remarks. Honorable Chairperson, finally, I just want to say this. This country belongs to all of us. Terai, hills, mountains, Mechi, Mahakali, people of all classes, regions, all religions, all cultures, if we walk with arrogance, with ego, with pride, saying I have such a large number, then somewhere we will stumble, somewhere we will get hurt. Therefore, the government must always walk with its eyes open, with its mind open, with its heart open. We have fallen into disaster many times due to the arrogance of thinking 'I am right', we have fallen. May that not happen again, may we all come together and engage in the campaign to build the nation. With this wish, may KP Oli and Ramesh Lekhak be freed, may the people get justice and fairness, may we see justice done. I wish you good luck, thank you, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (14:26 hrs) Honorable Shri Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):- First of all, I want to express my heartfelt tribute on behalf of my party, the Nepal Communist Party, to all the known and unknown martyrs who sacrificed their lives from 2007 BS to August 23/24, 2082 BS for the nation, nationality, republic, and good governance. I want to extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the newly elected honorable members of the National Assembly and the House of Representatives. I also wish them a successful tenure. Similarly, we have formed a new government. I want to extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the honorable ministers of this government. I also wish them a successful tenure. In this context, we are present on the first day of the 20th session of the National Assembly today. In this context, I want to extend my best wishes for the historical and grand success of the 20th session. Honorable Chairperson, the system we are in today, this democratic federal republican system, was not achieved easily. We have made great sacrifices for it, the Nepali people have made sacrifices. Therefore, my party, the Communist Party of Nepal, is always committed to the republic, federalism, secularism, and inclusivity achieved through these sacrifices. I also want to request this here. Honorable Chairperson, as we all know, we are located in a complex geography. We are in a situation where there are countries with vast geographies, competing in terms of development. In such a situation, we have the challenge of how to move forward in a unique way while preserving Nepal's nationality and its distinctiveness. I have taken a pledge, and I also want to express my pledge that this government, based on its own originality, will respect Nepal's republic, Nepal's democracy, Nepal's inclusivity, federalism, and secularism, and move forward by further enriching it. Honorable Chairperson, I don't need to elaborate here. Our country, which is economically and socio-culturally backward, if we look at the history of the world, has always been a laboratory for others. I feel that from 2007 BS until today, our country has also been a laboratory, and some people outside make such comments. I feel that the current government needs to be aware of this. All of us who love Nepal and are proud to be Nepali. I feel that we all need to be conscious, and in this regard, the policy we have adopted, the policy of moving forward based on the principle of pragmatism, must be maintained firmly and we must move forward with it. The Rastriya Swatantra Party has achieved an unprecedented victory in the recent elections. The government has also announced its 100-day agenda, which I welcome. However, I could not find in it how to remove the irregularities in education, how to end the irregularities in foreign employment, how to manage the many possibilities for our youth returning from foreign employment due to the ongoing war, how to bring back those at risk, and consequently, how to manage and control the rising inflation due to the fuel shortage caused by the war. I could not find these in the 100-point agenda. I also feel that other public interest issues have not been included. There is no mention of the agricultural sector. We know that our health is being compromised even now. We are forced to eat food mixed with pesticides. I feel that we need to be sensitive about this. I feel that the seeds we are currently using in the agricultural sector are not productive seeds. If there is a blockade tomorrow and we are not given seeds, there is a growing danger that we will not be able to produce anything in our country. We need to be aware of this in time, the government needs to be aware, I feel. And I want to request that Nepal, a small country, needs to be aware that monopolies of multinational companies should not be established. Similarly, there is no mention of border area problems in the 100-day agenda, no mention of treaties and agreements, how to manage the diplomatic sector. We have seen many irregularities in the diplomatic sector, and how to manage them is also not found there. All these things would be like adding icing to the cake, I feel. I want to state that this democratic government should be able to work in accordance with the spirit of democracy. We are parties that believe in the rule of law, we are Nepalis. Is the republic, federalism, inclusivity, secularism that we have today achieved just like that? To achieve it, our elders, our leaders, have made great sacrifices. Many of our youths have sacrificed their lives. Many have disregarded their personal lives and fought for that democracy, for the republic. But today, is there a fear that democracy will be weakened? Will anarchy prevail? Will the parties and leaders who contributed to bringing the republic yesterday be subjected to injustice? Will this democratic government proceed through legal procedures or not?

It has been marked. The democratic government, which has been victorious in an unprecedented manner, must also remember that sacrifice, that sacrifice. It is necessary to remember that this has not happened just like that, and it is necessary to work towards respecting it, respecting democracy, and further enriching it, and that no action should be taken out of a spirit of revenge by violating laws and procedures. I want to state that clearly here. Honorable Chairperson, we are seeing that incidents of violence against women are increasing day by day. Just recently, we learned about Nisha BK, who was raped and murdered. I want to ask the government, the democratic government. How long will we have to protest at Maiti Ghar to get justice? Is it enough to light candles after death to get justice? We have to give justice to the people at the bottom, to the communities at the bottom. I want to request that the democratic government keep this in mind and think about it. We are currently seeing so much cyberbullying. Women cannot write anything, women cannot say anything. So much cyberbullying is happening. We are currently seeing that a young sister, Amisha Parajuli, has been subjected to so much bullying. If she were a normal person, she would be forced to commit suicide. She cannot develop her personality fearlessly and freely. I want to ask the democratic government, shouldn't the cyber bureau be automatically active? Why do we have to go and file a complaint? What is the situation? The democratic government should stop such things and ban them. An investigation should be conducted to bring the wrongdoers to justice, I think. The responsibility to protect the republic, democracy, inclusivity, and secularism lies with this government, Honorable Chairperson. Along with that, it is the desire and need of the Nepali people to develop Nepal on the path of prosperity according to their needs. Large projects need to be constructed. I want to request the government to operate the Shahid Dashrath Chand Health Sciences University in full phase from this financial year. Large projects like West Seti and Karnali should be constructed, and this government should work according to the aspirations of the people, the needs of the people, and the needs of the nation. And finally, I want to request again that institutional and systematic reforms must be made, but in the name of doing so, the state should not do any work in a way that takes revenge on anyone or destroys anyone. Transparency must be there, it must be done legally, procedurally, impartially, and I request that this government follow that path and that path. And with thanks for the time, I want to take leave. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal. (14:37 hrs) Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dahal (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable Chairperson, the Rastriya Swatantra Party has secured a majority in the House of Representatives elections held on Falgun 29th. I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to the leader of the party's parliamentary group and Honorable Prime Minister Mr. Balendra Shah. Similarly, I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes for a successful term to all the members of his cabinet. May this government be able to address the issues of the people's livelihood while maintaining the welfare of the Nepali people, the nation, nationality, national unity, independence, and territorial integrity. Our party will provide cooperation in this work. We are in opposition and we want to play a constructive role. Do good work, thank you very much. Do bad work, we will oppose it. Therefore, our party's perspective will be to look at this government based on merit and demerit. Honorable Chairperson, elections were held in all constituencies and all provinces of the country on Magh 11th. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the Honorable Members elected to the National Assembly. I wish you a successful term. Today, the Secondary Education Examination (SEE) has started. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the children, students, and examinees to achieve excellent marks and pass out. Honorable Chairperson, the first meeting of the newly formed Council of Ministers decided to implement the report of the "Gauri Bahadur Karki Commission" formed to investigate the loss of life and property in the demonstrations of Bhadra 23rd and 24th, and based on that decision, the arrest of the Chairman of the CPN UML and former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and the then Home Minister and leader of the Nepali Congress, Mr. Ramesh Lekhak, has drawn the serious attention of our party. It is clear how cruel and criminal the intentions of this government are? The personality who has been Prime Minister repeatedly, the Chairman of the CPN UML, has been arrested in an extremely insulting manner, and why has this government become so unruly? Why has it presented itself this way? Especially the elderly body of former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli, I completely agree with the two times. Honorable Krishna Prasad Sitoula has already raised it. A person who has undergone kidney transplantation twice and is suffering from a chronic illness. Even in this condition, his father's funeral ceremony was about to be completed, and while the rituals were still ongoing, this incident occurred. From midnight, all the roads and entry points around his residence were closed, and they waited at his doorstep and arrested him as if he were a terrorist. This government has done this. We express our regret for this. They were arrested based on the necessary documents and illegal orders. Is he a person who would leave the country? If he were to leave, it has been 7 months since the incident, he would have already left. He would not have fled. He is the ultimate protector of this country, we are all protectors, he is the ultimate protector. We feel so, otherwise, he would have been in some position and there would be no evidence. This arrest has been made unnecessarily. Our party strongly objects to, condemns, and denounces this arrest, which has been made in violation of all laws, legal procedures, and democratic values. Honorable Chairperson, our party was and is firm in the demand for an impartial investigation into the loss of life and property during the demonstrations of Bhadra 23, 2082, and for an impartial investigation into the infiltration that made the demonstration of Bhadra 24th destructive, and the attack, looting, and arson of national and private property. Without impartial investigation, the commission's chairman Gauri Bahadur Karki, before the commission was formed, tweeted as much as he wrote statuses, and presented conclusions. The report only serves to confirm those conclusions. There is nothing else in the report. The Karki Commission's role has been proven to be completely biased and prejudiced by not investigating other matters. Our party's view that this commission was not formed for impartial investigation is confirmed by its report. Therefore, our party concludes that this report has been prepared with the intention of characterizing the leadership's journey and institutionalizing the then political politics with prejudice. Hence, this report is condemnable and regrettable, and we reject all actions taken based on this report. Based on such a one-sided report based on false information, which is prejudiced and retaliatory, the Chairman of the CPN UML and former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak must be released unconditionally and immediately. They must be released unconditionally and immediately. I strongly demand this from our party. I propose that the chairman and members of the commission that brought such a baseless, prejudiced, and retaliatory report be investigated and punished. I demand their release, unconditional and immediate release, and punishment for the chairman and members of the Karki Commission and Karki Commission who brought such a report. Regarding the Karki Commission's report, the Council of Ministers' decision to proceed with action without studying the reactions of legal experts and civil society leaders is extremely retaliatory and objectionable. We express our regret for this decision of the government. What a paradox it is to form a study committee for the security personnel. It is clear how prejudiced and retaliatory the newly formed government is towards the opposition leaders, as it decides to form a committee selectively but moves towards implementation for the then political leadership. Honorable Chairperson, I want to bring to your attention that individuals involved in the incidents of forcing children in school uniforms onto the streets during the protest on Bhadra 23rd, creating a tense situation by surrounding them, spreading terror, and the incidents of arson and vandalism on the 24th at the Parliament building, Singha Durbar, Supreme Court, provincial and local government offices, security agency buildings, government offices, political party offices, private industries, and individuals' homes, should be brought under the legal framework through impartial and independent investigation. The act of taking action against the security personnel who used force to protect the Parliament building after being attacked and disarmed, and when the attack on the Parliament building began, is unfortunate. Similarly, any step taken without impartial investigation of all parties will be biased and prejudiced, and it will raise questions about the entire criminal justice system. Therefore, our party demands that the prejudiced Karki Commission's report be immediately scrapped. The Council of Ministers' decision of Chaitra 13th must be immediately withdrawn. A high-level judicial inquiry, impartial, independent, and neutral, led by a sitting judge of the Supreme Court, including experts, should be formed to analyze and investigate all the incidents of Bhadra 23rd and 24th. We are aware of all the attempts to arrest our party chairman in a retaliatory manner and frame him in false cases. We are seeking justice through all three fronts: the parliament, the streets, and the legal system. In this process, the central committee members, leaders, cadres, and honorable members of the CPN UML who participated in peaceful public mobilization have been brutally kicked in the chest. Initially, there was an attack on the party office, and a large number of people were injured. This has happened across the country. We condemn and denounce the government's oppressive policy. What a tragedy it is. We all made sacrifices to bring about the federal democratic republic. The right to speak, the right to write, the right to give speeches, the right to organize assemblies, the right to participate peacefully in processions, the right to protest, these are rights guaranteed by the constitution. These rights...

There are works being done to curb it. We are aware. Therefore, we demand that this kind of slanderous attack on our chairperson, which is unjust, biased, and vindictive, be immediately withdrawn, and for this, we have already come to the streets. We will present the party's statements and the people's views in the same way in the parliament. We will seek justice on the streets and legally. We feel that our voices are being heard, and in the end, truth will prevail. In the end, truth will prevail. I have presented the details above about what kind of personality it is. How was this government able to arrest him? How much injustice is there in a federal democratic republic? How can such a thing happen in such a system? It should not happen. Therefore, such things have happened, which are ironic and unfortunate. Therefore, it should be corrected immediately. I would like to reiterate and request again that former Prime Minister and leader of the Congress, the honorable Ramesh Lekhak, and the Chairman of NCP UML and Nepali Congress leader, KP Sharma Oli, be immediately released, and our demand is for a neutral, impartial, and judicial investigation led by a sitting Supreme Court judge into the overall incidents of the 23rd and 24th, and that strict action be taken against the culprits. Thank you, Namaste.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Puja Chaudhary.
(14:51 hrs)
Honorable Ms. Puja Chaudhary (People's Socialist Party Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, I would like to extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes for a successful tenure from my party, JSP Nepal, and on my personal behalf to all the Honorable Members of the National Assembly and the House of Representatives who have just been elected by the people's mandate. I also extend my warm congratulations to the new Prime Minister and all the members of the cabinet of our country. Indeed, our country is multilingual, multi-religious, multicultural, and geographically diverse, and this is the beauty of democracy. It is well known that the youth played a major role in the series of incidents that began nationwide from the 23rd and 24th of Bhadra, 2082 BS. The impact of that youth movement has directly affected public property, trade, industry, and daily wage laborers, and even now, the Nepali people feel a sense of insecurity somewhere. However, I would like to congratulate all the Honorable Members who won the elections on the 21st of Falgun, in accordance with the pain of those injured and martyred in the movement and the voice of the Nepali people against corruption and the demand for governance reform. You have reached this point by winning the immense love and trust of the people. This is not just a victory. It is also a great responsibility, and it is a challenge. The National Assembly also has a very important role in balancing this responsibility and challenge with the balance of power and the balance of skill and effectiveness. The rampant corruption in the country, misgovernance, the product of unemployment, this movement, and the majority government after the elections of Falgun 21, which is moving forward by embracing the path of anti-corruption, economic growth, and economic reform. We will also provide support and cooperation for bringing good governance to the country. We want the Nepali people to feel good governance. We want the youth to get employment opportunities in the country, and we want the country to take a new leap forward on the path of development and for everyone to experience a new Nepal. While bringing corrupt individuals to justice and taking action against them is a welcome step, the question of whether those who burn the country's physical government structures in the name of protest will be brought to justice, and why other state agencies remained silent when government structures were burned and destroyed, still remains unclear. In the name of the youth movement, whoever was injured, and some are still undergoing treatment. Those who lost everything, the families of the martyrs, their wounds may hardly be healed by anyone. Their tears, their pain may hardly be lessened by anyone. However, with the hope that their sacrifice was for positive change, I humbly request the current government to bring to justice anyone who is responsible for this. By making the hopes, expectations, desires, and trust of the Nepali people result-oriented, and expecting transparency, honesty, and support, our country Nepal and the Nepali people will move forward on the path of development, good governance, and prosperity. Once again, I congratulate all the Honorable Members elected to the National Assembly and all the Honorable Members of the House of Representatives and wish them a successful tenure. I also extend my best wishes to all the students participating in the SEE examination which begins today. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Mahanta Thakur.
(14:56 hrs)
(14:57 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Mahanta Thakur (Democratic Socialist Party, Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, I, we have just sung a national anthem, and I am having difficulty with the language here. Do I have to speak in my own language? A garland of a hundred flowers is Nepali. Now, we have various cultures and languages in this. Listening to all this, it feels very proud. But is this the reality? Flowers bloom for the forest; if they are not looked after, where will our nationality go? We have an army; only sovereign nations have armies. Therefore, we feel that we are truly a sovereign country. We have sovereignty in our country. Our sovereignty has not gone abroad. But is that also the reality? What is the reality? We have also heard that the situation we are in now is not something we have reached by chance. It has not been reached by anyone's boon or gift. We have reached this stage after fighting in the hundreds and thousands. But what is the situation today? People are still in jail today. They have been punished. We are witnessing the plight of many respected personalities. What is satisfying is that every ten years, there is a change here. Be it '97 BS, 2007 BS, 2017 BS, 2027 BS student movements, 2036 BS, and 2046 BS. The product of all this is the movement of 2062/63 BS; we are all products of 2062/63 BS, of that movement. So how much has changed? The face of the street looks black in some places. Temples and monasteries are also maintained. But what about the people? Why does this situation repeat every time? Because there is unemployment. Every 10 years, new youths are ready, and they have no employment. They have to go abroad. But even there, they come back with failed kidneys. Nowhere do we find protection; we call ourselves a nation. Have we truly Nepalis sacrificed for equality, freedom, and nationality? That's what we hear. But has equality truly come? Have we achieved freedom? It doesn't seem so. So where there is no freedom, where the sovereignty we talk about does not even exist. Then why live in such an unequal society? And they call us separatists. All these talk of separation, whoever comes to power. We hear the same language; their nationality. All rulers, when unity is threatened, when their power is threatened, give the slogan of nationality. To turn the people towards themselves, and this continues in a maze. History itself shows this; great empires have fallen, right before our eyes. In our country too, how many times has there been a "change" before this? The Lichhavis came, and now we have a republic. The republic has come, but they are secretly watching if they can get something again with your support. They won't get it, why would people take to the streets again? But that is visible. Attacks happened everywhere. On private commercial businesses, on businessmen, but nothing happened to Nirmal Niwas? The state power is visible there. Therefore, all those who talk about sovereignty are declining forces. They can give nothing but decay and stench. Now, the Honorable Chairperson has given me time, and you have listened. Thank you very much. Thank you. Jai Madhesh.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Tul Prasad Bishwakarma.
(15:04 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (National People's Front):- Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, Secretaries, and other attending staff. Today, we are in the first session of this new session. Standing here on the first day of this 20th session, I, and indeed all the Nepali people, are experiencing uncertainty about where the country is heading and what will happen. Certainly, we have a new government, and they have put forward some of their action plans. But all of them are incomplete. Policies and programs according to the needs of the country and the Nepali people have not come. Therefore, I feel that this democratic republic, brought about by the long struggle of the Nepali people against the Rana regime and the Panchayat system, will it receive justice or not? This is also a matter to consider. Because we have heard discussions about the Monroe Doctrine within the parliament itself, and we have also heard the proposal to reduce the size of the Nepali army within the parliament. Today, are those things still in place, or did we come to power by setting them aside? This is also a matter to consider. Because we know about the Monroe Doctrine. Its implication is that because India is a vast country, Nepal will only listen to what India says and will have to accept its patronage. How the new government will take these ideas and move forward is something to watch. Therefore, the most important thing for the country is the protection of national identity, territorial integrity, and sovereignty, and the protection of the democratic republic. We must protect secularism. This is the main point. Can the new government function on this basis or not? That is the question. 

Similarly, the issue of the report of the recently formed investigation commission has been raised. Certainly, that investigation is one-sided and flawed. It has not been able to investigate the overall incident impartially. The rampage that occurred on the 24th, the burning and destruction of government offices, important institutions, private homes, and private property. Who was behind it? Should they not be investigated? Should those found guilty not be brought to justice? That has not been spoken about. Therefore, this report of the investigation commission is incomplete. Our party disagrees with it.

Whatever anomalies and distortions have existed in the country since yesterday, the widespread corruption, policy-level corruption, inflation, and the problems faced by the people in education, health, and their daily lives remain as they are. How will this government solve them? That remains to be seen in the coming days, and without addressing the fundamental basic problems of the country, the change of government alone cannot bring peace and order to the country. The country cannot progress. Primarily, we must focus on a self-reliant economy. We are currently under the grip of multinational companies. We have no production; we only have imports. Our productive, capable youth power is migrating abroad. We must retain them in the country and provide them with employment within the country.

We do not have a plan. Can this government address it? Only then can this country move forward, only then can this country see progress. There are various marginalized groups, various linguistic groups. Various communities have their own kinds of problems. Women have separate problems. This issue has already been raised, honorable members have raised it. Issues of violence against women, and on top of that, issues of Dalit oppression are increasing day by day. There is a situation where a law has not yet been made to implement Article 40 of the Constitution of Nepal, which was enshrined for the Dalits. This is a great irony. The Dalit community is suffering from untouchability, discrimination, and ethnic oppression. It remains to be seen how effectively this government will work to uplift them and provide them relief. Although no previous government has done this, it has apologized for the discrimination faced by the Dalit community from the state. That is a positive thing. That is a good thing, but an apology is not enough. They must also be provided relief. Programs must be brought to uplift their standard of living, and budget must be allocated to implement those programs. Only when a program with a definite budget comes will the door open for the upliftment of specific communities and classes. Therefore, this government has come amidst many such problems. Therefore, this government should not work in an overly excited manner based on its majority. It should work by properly understanding the needs of the Nepali people and Nepal. Specifically, I want to say that a imperialist war is raging in the world today. Iran is burning. Its people are in distress. This war will directly affect our country. Because of this, inflation is increasing in everything, and in the midst of global turmoil, our country's foreign policy must be balanced. If the non-aligned foreign policy is not strongly adhered to, this country cannot survive and can be swayed left or right. This is because we are situated between two giant neighboring countries. If we cannot balance our foreign policy properly today, there is a possibility of our country's existence being erased. Not only that, but during the previous government's tenure, we have already passed the MCC. Our party has been saying from the beginning that this MCC is not beneficial for Nepal, and it is heard that there is an effort to pass the SPP internally. If the SPP is also passed, it will be a great misfortune for the country. I want to alert this government to pay attention to this matter in time. Therefore, we must adopt a foreign policy of standing on our own feet without relying on any world powers, and this government should move forward by paying attention to the basic needs of various castes, classes, communities, and marginalized regions within the country and what kind of facilities and development we need to provide them, and it should understand the sentiments of the Nepali people. With this, I wish them well. Finally, I also wish well to the new honorable members elected to the National Assembly and all the honorable members elected to the House of Representatives. With this, I conclude my remarks. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, the discussion from the parties will conclude here. Honorable Members, letters regarding the formation of the Council of Ministers and the allocation of portfolios have been received from the Office of the President. I will now inform you of the contents of the said letters. a. "Honorable President Ram Chandra Paudel has appointed Honorable Member of the House of Representatives, Balendra Shah, as the Prime Minister of Nepal on Baisakh 13, 2082, in accordance with Article 76, Sub-article (1) of the Constitution of Nepal. (Mahadev Panta) Secretary 2082 Baisakh 13" b. "Honorable President Ram Chandra Paudel, on the recommendation of the Right Honorable Prime Minister Balendra Shah, in accordance with Article 76, Sub-article (9) of the Constitution of Nepal, has formed the Council of Ministers and allocated portfolios as follows from Baisakh 13, 2082. (Mahadev Panta) Secretary 2082 Baisakh 15" List of Portfolios: S.N. Name Surname Position 1. Mr. Balendra Shah Prime Minister 2. Dr. Swarnim Wagle Minister, Finance 3. Mr. Sudhan Gurung Minister, Home Affairs 4. Mr. Shishir Khanal Minister, Foreign Affairs 5. Mr. Sunil Lamshal Minister, Physical Infrastructure and Transport; Urban Development 6. Mr. Biraj Bhakta Shrestha Minister, Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation 7. Mr. Khadga Raj Poudel Minister, Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation 8. Mr. Samit Pokharel Minister, Education, Science and Technology; Youth and Sports 9. Ms. Nisha Mehta Minister, Health and Population; Water Supply 10. Dr. Bikram Timilsina Minister, Federal Affairs and General Administration; Land Management 11. Ms. Pratibha Rawal Minister, Cooperatives and Poverty Allevitation 12. Ms. Sobita Gautam Minister, Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs 13. Ms. Gita Chaudhary Minister, Agriculture and Livestock Development; Forest and Environment 14. Mr. Deepak Kumar Sah Minister, Labor, Employment and Social Security 15. Ms. Sita Badi Minister, Women, Children and Senior Citizens. Honorable Members, in accordance with Rule (8) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I have scheduled the election for the post of Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly for Monday, Baisakh 23, 2082. Furthermore, in accordance with the provisions of the Rules, I direct the Secretary-General of the Federal Parliament, Padam Prasad Pandey, to publish the notice regarding the election program for the Vice-Chairperson. Honorable Members, in accordance with Rule 150 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, I have scheduled the election for the vacant chairpersons of the thematic committees of the National Assembly for Monday, Baisakh 24, 2082. Furthermore, I direct the Secretary of the National Assembly, Tul Bahadur Kandel, to publish the notice regarding the election program for the committee chairpersons. Honorable Members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Sunday, Baisakh 22, 2082, at 12:15 PM. This meeting is hereby adjourned. (Thereafter, the next meeting will be held on Sunday, Baisakh 22, 2082, at 12:15 PM. This meeting is hereby adjourned.) Adjourned: 15:19.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The 20th session of the National Assembly commenced with the Chairperson welcoming the members. The President's notification convening the session was read out, followed by a minute of silence to honor the martyrs. The Chairperson welcomed the newly elected members and reflected on the National Assembly's role in past political transitions.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Opening remarks, welcoming members, and reflecting on past sessions

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The Chairperson discussed the recent political changes, including the formation of a new government under Prime Minister Balendra Shah, and emphasized the importance of public mandate and government accountability. The need for cooperation between the House of Representatives and the National Assembly was highlighted, along with challenges related to the parliament building. The Chairperson also mentioned the upcoming orientation for new members and expressed hope for constructive debates.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Political changes, government accountability, parliamentary cooperation, and future expectations

sections.name: Statements by Party Representatives
sections.summary_en: Hon'ble Member Krishna Prasad Sitaula congratulated the newly elected members and wished the new government success, pledging constructive support. He also raised concerns about the government's first cabinet decision regarding the commission's report, questioning its adherence to due process and constitutional spirit.

speakers.name: Krishna Prasad Sitaula
speakers.topic: Congratulations, government support, and concerns about cabinet decision

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker emphasizes the importance of social harmony, national unity, and inclusive development. They highlight the need for the government to act with sensitivity and understanding, particularly in addressing the plight of citizens abroad and the ongoing challenges of unemployment and economic instability. The speaker also calls for a united approach to nation-building, warning against the potential for renewed conflict if such unity is not achieved.

speakers.name: KP Oli
speakers.topic: Prime Minister's health and legal proceedings

speakers.name: Ramesh Lekhak
speakers.topic: Justice and national unity

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" pays tribute to martyrs and congratulates newly elected members and ministers. She stresses the importance of the current democratic federal republican system, achieved through sacrifice, and reaffirms her party's commitment to its core principles. She also raises concerns about Nepal's economic and social backwardness, the need to avoid becoming a laboratory for others, and the importance of a pragmatic approach to governance.

speakers.name: Madan Kumari Shah "Garima"
speakers.topic: Tributes, congratulations, and national principles

key_issues: Congratulations to new members and ministers

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker critiques the government's 100-day agenda, noting the absence of specific plans for education, foreign employment, managing returning migrant workers, and controlling inflation. Concerns are raised about food safety, the quality of agricultural seeds, and the potential monopoly of multinational corporations. The speaker also points out the lack of focus on border issues, treaties, and diplomatic sector management within the agenda.

speakers.name: Madan Kumari Shah "Garima"
speakers.topic: Critique of government's 100-day agenda

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker questions whether the current democratic system, achieved through significant sacrifice, is being weakened or if anarchy will prevail. They express concern about potential injustice towards parties and leaders who contributed to the republic and seek assurance that the democratic government will proceed according to legal procedures.

speakers.name: Madan Kumari Shah "Garima"
speakers.topic: Concerns about democratic system and rule of law

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: A member raised concerns about increasing violence against women, including rape and murder, and criticized the government's slow response to providing justice. They also highlighted the issue of cyberbullying against women and urged the government to take proactive measures. The speaker also called for the operation of Shahid Dashrath Chand Health Sciences University and the construction of large projects like West Seti and Karnali, emphasizing the need for transparency and impartiality in government actions.

speakers.name: Honorable Member
speakers.topic: Violence against women, cyberbullying, and national development projects

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Prem Prasad Dahal congratulated the newly elected Prime Minister and his cabinet, pledging constructive opposition support. He also extended congratulations to the newly elected National Assembly members and wished students success in their SEE exams. The speaker strongly condemned the arrest of former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and former Home Minister Ramesh Lekhak, calling it politically motivated, retaliatory, and a violation of democratic principles. He criticized the Karki Commission's report as biased and demanded the immediate release of the arrested leaders and an investigation into the commission's leadership.

speakers.name: Prem Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Congratulations to new PM, condemnation of arrests, criticism of Karki Commission

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker continued to condemn the arrest of political leaders, criticizing the Karki Commission's report as prejudiced and retaliatory. They demanded the immediate release of KP Sharma Oli and Ramesh Lekhak and called for an investigation and punishment for the commission's members. The speaker also condemned the government's decision to proceed with actions based on the report without proper study and highlighted the selective nature of the government's actions. They further demanded an impartial investigation into the events of Bhadra 23rd and 24th, including the use of force by security personnel and the actions of protesters, and called for the scrapping of the Karki Commission's report and the withdrawal of the Council of Ministers' decision.

speakers.name: Honorable Member
speakers.topic: Condemnation of arrests, biased report, demand for investigation and release

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: A member expressed concern over attacks on the chairperson and demanded immediate withdrawal of slanderous attacks, calling for legal and street protests. Another member congratulated newly elected officials and discussed the country's diversity, the impact of recent protests, and the need for good governance and economic reform. A third member reflected on the nation's history, the struggle for democracy, and the persistent issues of unemployment and inequality, questioning the reality of sovereignty. The final member raised concerns about the direction of the country under the new government, the incomplete nature of policies, and the need to protect national identity, territorial integrity, and secularism, while also criticizing the one-sided investigation report and the ongoing corruption and unemployment.

speakers.topic: Protest against attacks on chairperson, demand for withdrawal and justice

sections.summary_en: A member expressed concerns about the government's plan to address the needs of marginalized communities, women, and Dalits, emphasizing the need for concrete programs and budget allocation. The member also warned against foreign policy entanglements like MCC and SPP, urging a balanced and independent foreign policy. The session concluded with the announcement of the formation of a new cabinet and the scheduling of elections for the Vice-Chairperson and committee chairpersons.
